config.title: Controlled Input

intro.title: Controlled Input
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple form with a text input field that displays the typed text in real-time. You'll learn how to create controlled inputs in Vue by binding form elements to component data. The main technologies involved are Vue's v-model directive for two-way data binding and reactive data properties. This approach ensures the input field and your component's data stay synchronized, giving you full control over form state.
intro.usecase: Controlled inputs are essential for building interactive forms in real-world applications like user registration, login screens, and checkout processes. They enable immediate validation and feedback in dashboards where users filter data or adjust settings, ensuring the UI always reflects the current state. This pattern is crucial for maintaining data consistency in complex interfaces like admin panels, configuration tools, and real-time collaborative editors.

objectives: Initialize reactive data properties to store input values in Vue components
Bind input elements to reactive data using v-model directive
Implement controlled input components that synchronize user input with component state
Configure event handlers to manipulate input data in response to user interactions
Construct forms with multiple controlled inputs that maintain synchronized state
Update component templates to render dynamic content based on controlled input values
Integrate controlled inputs with computed properties to transform user input data

steps.title: Import Vue and ref
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both Vue and ref from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a module
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue framework and ref function are available for use in the component.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named ControlledInputExample with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a component using the defineComponent function from Vue. The setup function should return an object (even if empty for now).
steps.seedCode:
import { defineComponent, ref } from 'vue';

// Create a Vue component named ControlledInputExample with a setup function
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named ControlledInputExample is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object.
successCriteria: The component is named ControlledInputExample, uses defineComponent, has a setup function, and returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've named the component ControlledInputExample, used defineComponent, and have a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a Vue component named ControlledInputExample with a setup function that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the component's setup function, initialize a reactive state variable named 'inputValue' using ref with an empty string as the initial value.
steps.hint: Use the ref function imported from Vue to create reactive state. Remember to call ref() with the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating reactive state
const message = ref('Hello');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a reactive state variable 'inputValue' initialized to an empty string.
successCriteria: The setup function contains a const declaration of 'inputValue' initialized with ref('').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using ref() with an empty string as the argument, and the variable should be named 'inputValue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a reactive state variable named 'inputValue' using the ref function with an empty string initial value.

steps.title: Define input handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleInput that takes an event parameter and updates inputValue with the event's target value.
steps.hint: Create a function that receives the event and sets inputValue.value to event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleInput function is defined that will update the reactive inputValue when called with an input event.
successCriteria: The handleInput function is defined in the setup function, takes an event parameter, and sets inputValue.value to event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it updates inputValue.value with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleInput function isn't defined correctly. It should take an event parameter and update inputValue.value.

steps.title: Return reactive state and handler
steps.instruction: In the setup function's return statement, return an object containing the inputValue ref and the handleInput function so they can be used in the template.
steps.hint: The return statement should expose both the state and handler as properties of an object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The setup function now returns an object with inputValue and handleInput, making them reactive and accessible in the template.
successCriteria: The return statement contains an object with both inputValue and handleInput properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both inputValue and handleInput are included in the returned object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The setup function should return an object containing both inputValue and handleInput. Check that you've included both properties.

steps.title: Add template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template section with a div container inside your component's return object.
steps.hint: In Vue, the template is returned from the setup function. Add a template property with a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a basic template structure with a div container.
successCriteria: The return object includes a template property containing a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding a template property to the return object with a div element inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't quite right. Remember to add a template property with a div element to the return object.

steps.title: Add input element
steps.instruction: Inside the template's div, add a text input element with type='text'.
steps.hint: Use the <input> tag with the type attribute set to 'text'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a text input element
<input type="text" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a text input field.
successCriteria: An <input> element with type='text' is present inside the div in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an input element, but make sure it has type='text' attribute.
steps.feedbackWrong: The text input element is missing or incorrect. Add <input type="text"> inside the div.

steps.title: Bind input value to state
steps.instruction: In the template, bind the input element's value to the inputValue ref using v-bind:value or :value.
steps.hint: Use v-bind:value or its shorthand :value to connect the input's value attribute to your reactive state.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example: binding an input to a ref -->
<input :value="message" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element will have its value bound to the inputValue ref, establishing one-way data flow from state to input.
successCriteria: The input element includes :value or v-bind:value attribute bound to inputValue.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using :value or v-bind:value to bind the input's value attribute to inputValue.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input value isn't properly bound to state. Use :value or v-bind:value to connect the input to inputValue.

steps.title: Wire input event to handler
steps.instruction: Add the @input event listener to the input element to call the handleInput function when the input value changes.
steps.hint: Use Vue's @input directive (or v-on:input) on the input element to bind the handleInput function to the input event.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: binding an event handler to an input
<input @input="handleChange" />
steps.expectedOutcome: The input element should have an @input attribute that calls the handleInput function when the user types.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the @input directive to the input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element doesn't have an event listener yet. Try adding @input="handleInput" to the input element.

steps.title: Display current input value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the input that displays the current input value using Vue's template syntax.
steps.hint:
Use the

tag and reference the inputValue reactive state inside double curly braces.
steps.analogousExample:
// Display reactive state in template

Current value: {{ inputValue }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The input value will be displayed in real-time below the input field as the user types.
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists in the template that displays the current value of inputValue using Vue's template syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it correctly references the inputValue reactive state using double curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element is missing or doesn't correctly display the inputValue. Remember to use Vue's template syntax with double curly braces.
